objective: Define the canonical shared ingredient schema and taxonomy using ICF-01 reconciliation evidence: stable identity/alias/provenance, physical/ecological/agricultural/economic/culinary/magical-culinary/alchemical profiles, units, rarity/classification mappings, quality/condition overlays, substitution groups, lifecycle and validation rules while preserving MIB-12 crafting, MIB-13 economy and creature-authority boundaries.
implementation_decisions: Canonical IDs are manually governed and immutable after publication; lexical normalization is candidate discovery only and never identity authority.
Primary ingredient IDs use ingredient:<slug>; reusable processed ingredient-like intermediates reserve preparation:<slug> for ICF-10; finished recipe outputs remain their owning item/content kind.
Canonical rarity, nature/origin classification, acquisition availability and MIB-13 market scarcity are separate dimensions.
Canonical rarity bands are common, uncommon, rare, exceptional, legendary and unique; source mappings retain the exact source term and semantic context.
Alchemy Exotic maps to exceptional only because Alchemy explicitly uses Exotic as a rarity tier; Agriculture Exotic/Supernatural remain source classification assertions unless separately reconciled.
Legacy prices/values are provenance-scoped source assertions only; MIB-13 remains authoritative for current market prices and scarcity.
Units are explicit typed quantity units; conversions require explicit exact rational rules and generic Food/Material/resource units remain unresolved source-unit assertions until ICF-13.
Quality and condition are live-state overlays owned with the Asset instance; ingredient definitions may declare allowed overlay/effect rules but not current instance quality/condition.
Creature-source fields may reference only authored creature biology/harvest evidence; absence remains a coverage gap.
Substitution is an explicit typed relation and never changes canonical identity.
completion_gate: A provider-neutral canonical ingredient schema and taxonomy resolves ICF-01 open decisions explicitly, preserves source vocabularies/provenance, distinguishes rarity/classification/availability/market scarcity, defines stable identity/alias/unit/profile/overlay/substitution/lifecycle rules, and supports later plant/animal/magical/derived/recipe/harvest content without a parallel live-state ledger. Machine-readable schema, taxonomy/source mappings and conformance examples must be repository-health clean.
